q1_what_did_you_play: Both energy into damage: Sounding Line at the Sludge Spinner first (spending 6 of my 8 Charge for 12 damage and Hydro), then Water's Edge at it for 6 more. That is 18 damage, taking the Spinner from 34 to 16, and leaves me 2 Charge. I take the telegraphed 8 unblocked and end at 40/70. I played Sounding Line first purely so the Charge spend happens while I still hold it; nothing else in the hand competes for Charge.
q2_other_line_considered: Two. Sounding Line plus Coral Guard — 12 damage and 5 Block, eating only 3 — was the one I actually weighed, and I rejected it because 5 Block buys less than the 6 damage Water's Edge gives when the incoming hit is 8 and I am at 48/70. Gyorin Formation alone (10 Block now, 6 next turn) I looked at and dismissed faster: it fully absorbs the 8 and banks more, but deals nothing, and against a 34 HP enemy on a clock I set myself, a zero-damage turn just buys the Spinner another swing at me later.
q3_what_it_gave_up: All defence. I ate the full 8 rather than turning any of it aside, so I am spending health as the resource this turn. It also empties most of my Charge — 8 down to 2 — so if a Charge-hungry card shows up next turn I cannot pay for it, and Gyorin Formation's start-of-next-turn 6 Block is a future cushion I chose not to bank. In exchange I am 18 damage further along and the Spinner is inside reach of a two-card finish.
q4_different_intent: Yes. The 8 is small enough that trading through it is clearly right; a much bigger telegraphed hit flips the turn. If the Spinner had shown something like 18 or more, Gyorin Formation becomes the play — the 10 Block plus 6 next turn actually pays for its 2 energy against a number that large. A telegraphed block or buff on the enemy instead of an attack would have pushed me the same way I went, only harder: all damage, and I would not have thought about Coral Guard at all. A defensive or non-damaging intent from the enemy would also make Coral Guard strictly wasted.
